title: As a founder, I can run a SOC 2 program end to end — Type I and Type II — with the Trust Services controls, required policies, and evidence requests built into the platform
As a security engineer, ISO 27001 is a first-class framework — the current Annex A control set, Statement of Applicability, and certification-audit artifacts are supported, not just mapped
As an operations lead, frameworks beyond SOC 2 and ISO — HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS — are supported from the same platform so new customer requirements don't mean a new tool
As a security engineer, controls and evidence map ACROSS frameworks — work done for SOC 2 counts toward ISO 27001 and HIPAA automatically, with the overlap shown
As a security engineer, I can add custom frameworks and custom controls with my own tests and evidence requirements alongside the built-in ones
As an IT admin, I can connect my real stack — cloud providers, identity, HR, code hosting, MDM, ticketing — through a documented integrations catalog with read-only scopes
As a security engineer, evidence is collected automatically from connected systems on a schedule — screenshots and CSV exports are replaced by timestamped, machine-gathered artifacts
As an operations lead, evidence that can't be automated has a real workflow — owners, due dates, renewal reminders, and expiry tracking on every manual artifact
As a developer, I can build private/custom integrations against a documented API to push evidence and test results from systems the catalog doesn't cover
As a security engineer, automated tests run continuously against my connected systems — failing controls surface within hours, not at the annual audit
As an IT admin, control failures and configuration drift alert me where I work — Slack, email, or ticketing — with enough context to fix the finding
As an IT admin, workstation compliance is tracked per employee — disk encryption, screen lock, password manager — via an agent or MDM integration
As an operations lead, third-party vendors are inventoried and risk-reviewed in the platform — security posture, data access, review cadence — instead of a spreadsheet
As a founder, my auditor works directly in the platform — a scoped auditor view of controls and evidence replaces email threads of PDFs
As a founder, I can book the audit itself through the vendor — a vetted auditor network or in-house audit arm with published expectations on timeline
As an operations lead, a readiness view shows exactly how far I am from audit-ready per framework — passing controls, open gaps, and what's left, as one honest percentage
As a sales lead, I get a hosted public trust center — live control status, certifications, and reports shared under click-through NDA — that closes security reviews before they start
As an operations lead, the trust center stays current on its own — subprocessor lists, document renewals, and control status update from the platform, not by hand
As a sales lead, security questionnaires get answered by AI from my actual controls and knowledge base — drafts I review, not blank spreadsheets I fill
As a sales lead, questionnaires arrive in every shape — SIG, CAIQ, portals, spreadsheets — and the platform imports and exports them in the format the customer sent
As a security engineer, a real risk register lives in the platform — scored risks, treatment plans, owners, and review cycles tied back to controls
As a founder, policies come from a lawyer-grade template library with an editor, versioning, approvals, and per-employee acceptance tracking
As an operations lead, security awareness training is built in — assigned on hire, tracked to completion, and accepted as audit evidence
As an IT admin, onboarding and offboarding are compliance events — HR-synced checklists prove every hire got training and every leaver lost access
As a security engineer, periodic user access reviews run across connected apps in the platform — reviewers sign off in-app and the artifact lands in the evidence library
